title: A signed degree-one cocycle on an augmented resolution is a coboundary
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $i:U\to I^\bullet$ and $j:V\to J^\bullet$ be injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions], indexed by $\mathbf N$. Suppose $E^n:I^n\to J^{n+1}$ and $e:U\to J^0$ satisfy $d_J^{n+1}E^n+E^{n+1}d_I^n=0$ and $E^0i=d_J^0e$. There exist $k^n:I^n\to J^n$ such that $k^0i=e$ and $d_J^nk^n-k^{n+1}d_I^n=E^n$ for every $n\geq0$.

proof.text: Extend e across the monic augmentation i into the injective object J^0 using Injective.factorThru. This gives k^0 with i ≫ k^0 = e.
Compatibility gives i ≫ (k^0 ≫ d_J^0 - E^0) = 0. Apply I.exact₀.descToInjective to extend this map across d_I^0 into J^1, giving k^1 with d_I^0 ≫ k^1 = k^0 ≫ d_J^0 - E^0.

Given k^n and k^{n+1} with the last identity, the cocycle identity and d_J^n ≫ d_J^{n+1} = 0 show d_I^n ≫ (k^{n+1} ≫ d_J^{n+1} - E^{n+1}) = 0. Use I.exact_succ n and Exact.descToInjective to obtain k^{n+2}. Dependent Nat recursion on pairs of consecutive maps retains the identity at each degree. Extract the first coordinate at every index and rearrange the subtraction to obtain the claimed formula.

from.place: Step 5 of injective restriction acyclicity: the horseshoe naturality argument, removal of the differential and augmentation defects

lean.statement: theorem horseshoe_defect_homotopy {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] {U V : C} (I : InjectiveResolution U) (J : InjectiveResolution V) (E : ∀ n : ℕ, I.cocomplex.X n ⟶ J.cocomplex.X (n + 1)) (e : U ⟶ J.cocomplex.X 0) (hE : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ≫ J.cocomplex.d (n + 1) (n + 2) + I.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) ≫ E (n + 1) = 0) (he : I.ι.f 0 ≫ E 0 = e ≫ J.cocomplex.d 0 1) : ∃ k : ∀ n : ℕ, I.cocomplex.X n ⟶ J.cocomplex.X n, I.ι.f 0 ≫ k 0 = e ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, k n ≫ J.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) - I.cocomplex.d n (n + 1) ≫ k (n + 1) = E n
